Title: Techno-Economic Analysis of Ammonia Cracking for Aviation Applications
Biography: I am an undergraduate at Carnegie Mellon University studying Chemical Engineering with an additional major in Computational and Applied Mathematics, and I am currently an exchange student at Imperial College London. My research interests include process systems engineering, techno-economic analysis, optimization, and sustainable energy and separation systems. At AISL, I have worked on techno-economic modeling of ammonia-based hydrogen supply and cracking for aviation applications using Aspen HYSYS and Python. My broader research experience includes rare-earth recovery, solvent extraction, and process optimization.
